$comment: The loop's control surface. Read by loop-tick.yml (the reactor), by
scripts/loop-blast-radius.mjs (the contagion firewall), and by
scripts/gen-loop-data.mjs (which publishes it, minus nothing — there are
no secrets here and the whole point is that the governor is public).
`enabled` is the master switch and it is OFF. Every loop workflow checks it
first and exits 0. Turning it on is a deliberate, reviewable commit — the
same shape as ANNOUNCE in bsky-hello.yml and BOT_ENABLED in the factory,
and for the same reason: the expensive, irreversible half of this system
should start with a diff someone signed.
The budget is the controller, not a limit (CLOSED-LOOP.md §8). The
reactor reads these and decides where the marginal turn pays; it does not
merely count down. `hardStopTurns` is the backstop that exists because a
controller with a bug is still a loop.
These numbers are guesses. Phase 1's second job is to replace them with a
measurement — the estimate in CLOSED-LOOP.md §10 is flagged there as the
weakest number in the document, and it still is.
ALL THREE ARE STOP CONDITIONS, and a loop that cannot stop is the failure
mode rather than the feature (CLOSED-LOOP.md §6.2). `noImprovementTurns`
is the interesting one: it is the measurement this whole programme exists
to take, wired up as a brake.
Three signals, deliberately not one model call. Disagreement between them
is itself data (CLOSED-LOOP.md §6.2). `weights` are placeholders until the
pilot's human scores calibrate them — an uncalibrated judge is a number,
not a measurement, and publishing it as one would be the exact mistake
this repo keeps writing down.
